source_text: Sic enim et in illo opere, quod Romam misisti, disputas: Voluntas, quae libera in malis est, libera in bonis non est [n161] .
pass_a_gloss: For thus also in that work which you sent to Rome you dispute: The will, which is free in evils, is not free in goods.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS liber=free; also children; context decides

pass_b_english: For in the work you sent to Rome you argue this way too: ‘The will, which is free in evil things, is not free in good things’ (Augustine, Against Two Letters of the Pelagians 1.7).

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at this locus; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
